LESSON: READING 2.2.1 READING FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to read fluently?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the meaning of intonation and pause in reading for expression
2. read texts using the right intonation and pause for expression

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 2.2.1 READING FLUENCY
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 2.2.1 READING FLUENCY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Explain the meaning of intonation and pause in reading for expression

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the meaning of intonation and pause in reading for expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the meaning of intonation and pause in reading for expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the meaning of intonation and pause in reading for expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read texts using the right intonation and pause for expression

What this means
In this part you learn to read texts using the right intonation and pause for expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read texts using the right intonation and pause for expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read texts using the right intonation and pause for expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain the meaning of intonation and pause in reading for expression)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency to a partner. (skill: read texts using the right intonation and pause for expression)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the meaning of intonation and pause in reading for expression.
3. Practise this skill: read texts using the right intonation and pause for expression.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to read fluently?
2. How can one conserve the environment?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the meaning of intonation and pause in reading for expression.
5. Be able to: read texts using the right intonation and pause for expression.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
